LOUISIANA PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION
                     ORDER NUMBER 09-09-2026 (R-37339) (CORRECTED)1

                  LOUISIANA PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION, EX PARTE.

Docket No. R-37339, In re: Proposed amendments to Commission General Orders dated April
21, 1999, November 08, 1999, April 25, 2012, and March 16, 2021 and supersede General Order
dated May 30, 2008 and October 13, 2023, as well as establishment of rules for transporters of
waste and saltwater to coincide with recent amendments to intrastate motor carrier insurance
requirements.

                  (Decided at the August 12, 2026 Business and Executive Session.)


                                                     ORDER

Background and Procedural History
         The Louisiana Public Service Commission (“LPSC” or “Commission”) Staff (“Staff”)

opened this rulemaking to amend General Orders dated April 21, 1999,2 April 25, 2012,3 and

March 16, 2021,4 as well as establish rules for transporters of waste and saltwater to coincide with

recent amendments to intrastate motor carrier insurance requirements. After beginning its review

and revisions to the above referenced General Orders, Staff determined that the rulemaking should

be expanded to include General Orders dated November 08, 1999,5 October 13, 2023,6 and May

30, 20087 as all referenced General Orders include insurance requirements for common carriers

and motor carriers regulated by the Commission.


         Notice of this rulemaking was originally published in the Commission’s Official Bulletin

# 1329 dated August 02, 2024, and no parties intervened. This rulemaking was republished in the

Commission’s Official Bulletin # 1379 dated July 02, 2026 to provide additional opportunity for

General Order issued on September 9, 2026.

Transportation. (“Charter Bus GO”)

for the United States Department of Defense to include affiliated companies on their Common Carrier Certificates
while operating under Tender of Service Agreements with the United States Department of Defense’s Non-temporary
Storage Program. (“HHG GO”)
5 Louisiana Public Service Commission, ex parte. In re: New Guidelines and Procedures for Wrecker and Towing

Services. (“Wrecker and Towing GO”)
6 Louisiana Public Service Commission, ex parte. In re: Possible amendments to General Order dated January 12,

7 Louisiana Public Service Commission, ex parte. In re: Discussion and possible vote at the May 14, 2008 B&E, on

amending General Order dated June 30, 1974, establishing minimum liability insurance coverage for common
carriers transporting 12 passengers or less and those common carriers transporting 5 passengers or less, evaluating
the present liability insurance requirements of said carriers, evaluating the availability of said coverage in the
insurance industry and generally reviewing all laws and regulations applicable to said carriers.(“Dispatch Taxi GO”)

                                                             Order No. 09-09-2026 (R-37339) (Corrected)
                                                                                                Page 1
 stakeholder input given the decision to include Commission General Orders dated November 08,

1999, October 13, 2023, and May 30, 2008. As discussed in more detail throughout the

recommendation, Staff recommended that certain Commission General Orders should be amended

to remove any insurance requirements included therein – placing said requirements into one rule

– and other Commission General Orders should be superseded by these rules, as those particular

General Orders only addressed insurance requirements. Staff recommended that the Commission

should maintain one General Order with rules attached that provide all insurance requirements for

jurisdictional common carriers and motor carriers. Staff filed its Recommendation on Proposed

Rules and Request for Comments on June 30, 2026 seeking comments on the proposed rules no

later than Monday, July 27, 2026 in order to prepare Final Rules for consideration at the

Commission’s August 2026 Business and Executive Session. Staff also published the proposed

rules in the Commission’s Official Bulletin # 1379, dated July 2, 2026 for additional opportunity

for intervention and to provide comments. No interventions, nor comments were received.



Jurisdiction and Applicable Law
       The Commission has been vested with the authority to regulate public utilities and common

carriers and exercises jurisdiction in this proceeding pursuant to Article IV, Section 21(b) of the

Louisiana Constitution of 1974, which provides in pertinent part:

            The commission shall regulate all common carriers and public utilities and
            have such other regulatory authority as provided by law. It shall adopt
            and enforce reasonable rules, regulations, and procedures necessary for
            the discharge of its duties, and shall have other powers and perform other
            duties as provided by law.

The Louisiana Supreme Court has repeatedly held that the above-referenced provision gives the

Commission exclusive, plenary power to regulate all common carriers and public utilities.

Furthermore, acts or omissions of the Legislature cannot subtract from the Commission's power.

Global Tel Link, Inc. v. Louisiana Public Service Commission, 97-0645, pp. 6-7 (La. 1/21/98),

707 So. 2d 28, 33; Bowie v. Louisiana Public Service Commission, 627 So. 2d 164 (La. 1993).

The Commission’s power in this regard is as complete in every respect as the regulatory power

that would have been vested in the legislature in the absence of Art. IV § 21 (B.) Bowie. Pursuant

to the Commission’s constitutional authority, the Commission has issued several General Orders

over the years related to common carriers, including the Commission’s requirements to obtain a




                                                    Order No. 09-09-2026 (R-37339) (Corrected)
                                                                                       Page 2
 common carrier certificate, which included minimum insurance requirements.8

         Along with this Constitutional authority, the Legislature has also provided the Commission

with regulatory authority over wreckers and towing services. La. R.S. 45:180.1 provides in

pertinent part: “the [C]ommission has power and authority necessary to supervise, govern,

regulate, and control the business of the operation and use of wreckers and towing services” and

the “power, authority, and duties of the [C]ommission shall include all matters connected with the

service to be given or rendered, [and] the records to be kept by persons engaged in said business.”

         In addition to providing the Commission with regulatory authority over wreckers and

towing services, the Legislature also attempted to provide definitions as to what is a common

carrier, and in doing so, created the concept of motor carrier. Motor Carriers, as defined by the

Legislature, “includes both a common carrier by motor vehicle and contract carrier by motor

vehicle, which transport household goods, passengers, waste intrastate, or any other classification

of carriers created by law which transports household goods, passengers, or waste intrastate for

compensation or hire.”9 The Legislature also included wrecking and towing services within its

definition of Motor Carriers.



Recent Legislative Amendments

         Notwithstanding Global Tel and Bowie, supra, the Legislature has amended certain

relevant Revised Statutes throughout the years associated with Motor Carriers and minimum

insurance requirements. The two revisions pertinent to this Rulemaking docket are Act 935 of the

2001 Legislative Session and Act 747 of the 2024 Legislative Session.

         Act No. 935 amended La R.S. 45:163(D)(1)(b), relative to vehicle towing and storage

services, including public liability and property damage insurance coverage requirements, which

set a five-hundred thousand dollars combined single limit as the minimum coverage. Act 747

amended La R.S. 45:163(D) relative to insurance and indemnity bonds. The main revisions

removed the requirement of a Cash on Delivery bond and required certain motor carriers to




8 See the Charter Bus GO, the Passenger GO, and the HHG GO.
9 See La. R.S. 45:162(12). As the regulatory agency with plenary authority over common carriers, the Commission is

not acquiescing any of its authority to the Louisiana Legislature as it relates to common carriers by referencing and
using the definition of motor carrier. The Commission recognizes this nomenclature has been used within the common
carrier industry for some time (dating back prior to the 1974 Louisiana Constitution), and to avoid additional confusion
within these rules, the Commission will continue to use motor carrier until such time as the La. Revised Statutes can
be amended. Throughout this recommendation, when Staff uses motor carrier, common carrier can, and should be,
read in its place.

                                                               Order No. 09-09-2026 (R-37339) (Corrected)
                                                                                                  Page 3
 maintain minimum insurance coverage, including minimum requirements for saltwater and waste

haulers.

Staff’s Analysis and Final Recommendation
        Given the current insurance requirements for Common Carriers and Motor Carriers are

housed throughout several General Orders, Staff recommended that the Commission adopt one set

of “Rules and Regulations” that would apply to the motor carrier industry as a whole. Specifically,

Staff proposed the Commission adopt a set of Commission “Rules and Regulations” on minimum

insurance requirements across all types of regulated Motor Carriers. The Commission has

previously adopted such “global rules and regulations” in other areas of Commission jurisdiction

(water and wastewater,10 telecommunications,11 correctional phones,12 and common carrier

pipelines13 to name a few). In each of these instances, efforts were made to codify, on a

Commission level consistent with the constitutional rulemaking authority, all rules and regulations

applicable to a particular industry or class of carriers.


In proposing the codification of minimum insurance requirements for Motor Carriers, Staff

recommended amendments to some Commission General Orders, other Commission General

Orders be superseded in their entirety, and proposed new rules for saltwater and waste hauler

Motor Carriers. Based upon Staff’s review of the relevant Commission General Orders, Staff

recommended modifications to current Commission General Orders, as well as new rules, all to be

codified in one Intrastate Motor Carrier Insurance Requirements Rule. Staff’s Recommendation

noted that having a single General Order codifying all insurance requirements for common

carriers/motor carriers makes the most sense in lieu of having multiple orders referencing similar

minimum requirements. Having all insurance requirements in one General Order allows greater

ease and accessibility for all common carriers/motor carriers seeking to ensure compliance with

the Commission’s rules. Further, as there are several Motor Carriers that currently maintain limits

lower than those in Staff’s Proposed Rules, Staff recommended allowing those carriers to obtain

the minimum insurance requirements, related to the company’s respective designation, upon the

renewal or replacement of their current insurance on file with the Commission.14


10 See Water and Wastewater Rules and Regulations, as most recently modified by the General Order dated September

12, 2014.
11 See Regulations for Competition in the Local Telecommunications Market, as most recently amended by the General

Order dated July 26, 2013
12 Inmate Calling Services Rules and Regulations, adopted by the General Order dated April 20, 2016.
13 Rules Applicable to Common Carrier Pipelines, adopted by the General Order dated March 9, 2015.
14 This grace period does not apply to wrecker and towing services as their minimum insurance requirements will not

change as a result of this rulemaking.

                                                            Order No. 09-09-2026 (R-37339) (Corrected)
                                                                                               Page 4
          Staff’s Proposed Rules accomplished the following:

     1. Adopted definitions for the various classifications of motor carriers and specifically
        codified them therein.

     2. Maintained the historical distinction between Common and Contract Carriers.

     3. Placed all minimum insurance requirements for the various classifications of motor carriers
        into one rule.

     4. Identified the specific type(s) of insurance required for each classification of motor carrier.

     5. Provided the Commission’s filing requirements for insurance purposes.

     6. Removed the classification of Dispatch Taxicab from the classification of motor carriers,
        and provided for a definition of Grandfathered Dispatch Taxicab for those that currently
        hold authority with the Commission.

     7. Provided the requirement that Grandfathered Dispatch Taxicab drivers are required to
        provide a valid state issued Class “E” driver’s license.

     8. Removed a motor carrier’s ability to self-insure.

     9. Provided set standards for minimum insurance and the violations that can be assessed
        should a motor carrier not adhere to the Commission’s rules and regulations.



        Consistent with the review and analysis summarized above, as well as in Staff’s

Recommendation on Final Proposed Rule filed into the record on August 4, 2026, Staff

recommended that the Commission adopt the Amended Final Rules attached thereto as Attachment

A.


Commission Consideration
     This matter was considered at the August 12, 2026 Business and executive Session. After

discussion, on motion of Vice Chairman Coussan, seconded by Chairman Skrmetta, with

Commissioner Lewis concurring, Commissioner Francis temporarily absent, and Commissioner

Campbell absent, the Commission voted to adopt Staff’s Proposed Recommendation filed into the

record on August 4, 2026.



IT IS THEREFORE ORDERED THAT:

        Staff’s Proposed Recommendation filed into the record August 4, 2026, is adopted to,


     1. Remove the insurance requirements in General Orders dated April 21, 1999,

        November 08, 1999, April 25, 2012, and March 16, 2021;



                                                      Order No. 09-09-2026 (R-37339) (Corrected)
                                                                                         Page 5
    2. Codify minimum insurance requirements for Saltwater & Waste Carriers;


   3. Supersede General Order dated October 23, 2023 and adopt, new insurance rules as

       reflected in Attachment A hereto;


   4. Prohibit Motor Carriers from being self-insured and allow Motor Carriers who

       currently have a self-insured certificate on file to obtain the appropriate minimum

       insurance requirements related to the company’s respective designation upon

       expiration of their current self-insurance polices;


   5. Supersede General Order dated May 30, 2008 to remove Dispatched Taxicabs from

       the classification of motor carriers; and,


   6. Provide that Grandfathered Dispatch Taxicab drivers, as defined in Attachment A

       hereto, are no longer required to provide a Chauffeurs License or CDL but instead

       are required to provide a valid state issued Class “E” driver’s license.




This Order is effective immediately.


BY ORDER OF THE COMMISSION
BATON ROUGE, LOUISIANA
September 9, 2026

     Rules for common carriers related to minimum insurance requirements for

SECTION 101: PURPOSE

The Louisiana Public Service Commission hereby promulgates the following rules to exercise its
jurisdiction and authority over common carriers, specifically motor carriers, related to minimum
insurance requirements. In doing so, these rules amend General Orders dated April 21, 1999,15
November 08, 1999,16 April 25, 2012,17 and March 16, 2021,18 as well as supersede in its entirety
General Orders dated May 30, 200819 and October 13, 2023.20

SECTION 102: AUTHORITY

The Commission’s jurisdiction over common carriers and public utilities is established by Article
4, Section 21 of the Louisiana Constitution of 1974, which provides in pertinent part:

         The commission shall regulate all common carriers and public utilities and have
         such other regulatory authority as provided by law. It shall adopt and enforce
         reasonable rules, regulations, and procedures necessary for the discharge of its
         duties, and shall have other powers and perform other duties as provided by law.

The Louisiana Supreme Court has repeatedly held that the above-referenced provision gives the
Commission exclusive, plenary power to regulate all common carriers and public utilities.
Furthermore, acts or omissions of the Legislature cannot subtract from the Commission's power.
Global Tel Link, Inc. v. Louisiana Public Service Commission, 97-0645, pp. 6-7 (La. 1/21/98),
707 So. 2d 28, 33; Bowie v. Louisiana Public Service Commission, 627 So. 2d 164 (La. 1993).
The Commission’s power in this regard is as complete in every respect as the regulatory power
that would have been vested in the legislature in the absence of Art. IV § 21 (B.) Bowie. Pursuant
to the Commission’s constitutional authority, the Commission has issued several General Orders
over the years related to common carriers, including minimum requirements to obtain a common
carrier certificate, including minimum insurance requirements.21

Along with this Constitutional authority, the Legislature has also provided the Commission with
regulatory authority over wreckers and towing services. La. R.S. 45:180.1, provides in pertinent
part: “the [C]ommission has power and authority necessary to supervise, govern, regulate, and
control the business of the operation and use of wreckers and towing services” and the “power,
authority, and duties of the [C]ommission shall include all matters connected with the service to
be given or rendered, [and] the records to be kept by persons engaged in said business.”

SECTION 103. DEFINITIONS

    1. Commission/LPSC- The Louisiana Public Service Commission.

    2. Charter Bus- A passenger carrier with a seating capacity of 16 or more and
       is engaged or hired by a particular organization or group of persons for their
       exclusive use for a specific purpose or journey, or during a specific period
       of time. This definition does not include regular route buses.

    3. Common Carrier by Motor Vehicle - Means any person, other than a charter
       bus, the essential nature of whose business comprises engaging in,
       soliciting, or accepting household goods, passengers, saltwater, or waste,
       for intrastate transportation for hire, charge, or compensation as an
       employment or holding himself out as so available to the public generally
       and indiscriminately for such business.

             a. Passengers- A Common Carrier by Motor Vehicle who provides
                nonscheduled charter passenger service using vehicles which meet
                manufacturer’s specifications for no more than fifteen (15)
                passengers.

             b. Grandfathered Dispatch Taxicab- A Common Carrier by Motor
                Vehicle who only provides dispatched taxicab services using
                vehicles which meet manufacturer’s specifications for no more than
                ten (10) passengers and operate outside the parish of domicile or
                more than ten miles outside the corporate limits of an incorporated
                municipality. In order to meet this definition, a carrier’s Common
                Carrier Certificate must have been granted on or before General
                Order No. dated 9-9-2026 (R-37339).

             c. Household Goods- A Common Carrier by Motor Vehicle whose
                business transports:
                     i. Personal effects and property used, or to be used, in a dwelling when the
                        personal effects and property are a part of the equipment or supply of such
                        dwelling;
                    ii. Furniture, fixtures, equipment, and the property of stores, offices, museums,
                        institutions, hospitals, or other establishments, including all property
                        located within the establishment; ;
                  iii. Articles, including objects of art, displays, and exhibits, which, because of
                        their unusual nature or value, require specialized handling and equipment
                        usually employed in moving household goods; or
                   iv. Any goods listed above for an amount greater than $250.00.

             d. Saltwater- A Common Carrier by Motor Vehicle whose service is
                to transport saltwater utilized in oil well exploration and production
                intrastate.

         b. Saltwater - A Contract Carrier by Motor Vehicle whose service is to

         c. Waste - A Contract Carrier by Motor Vehicle whose service is to

SECTION 104. MINIMUM INSURANCE REQUIREMENTS

  A. Charter Buses are required to have minimum insurance coverage of:
        a. Two hundred fifty thousand dollars ($250,000) for injury or death
            to any one person not to exceed five hundred thousand dollars
            ($500,000) per occurrence; and
        b. Property damage insurance providing coverage of twenty-five
            thousand dollars ($25,000).
        c. In lieu of having (a) and (b) above as separate policies, the
            Commission will accept a minimum of five hundred and twenty-five
            thousand dollars ($525,000) combined single limits coverage for
            injury or death to any one person per occurrence for public liability
            and property damage insurance.

  B. Common and Contract Carriers of Passengers are required to have a
     minimum coverage of:
        a. Two hundred fifty thousand dollars ($250,000) for injury or death
           to any one person, not to exceed five hundred thousand dollars
           ($500,000) per occurrence;
        b. Property damage insurance providing coverage of at least twenty-
           five thousand dollars ($25,000).
        c. In lieu of having (a) and (b) above as separate policies, the
           Commission will accept a minimum of five hundred and twenty-five
           thousand dollars ($525,000) combined single limits coverage for
           injury or death to any one person per occurrence for public liability
           and property damage insurance.

  C. Grandfathered Dispatch Taxicab Carriers are required to have a minimum
     coverage of:
        a. Twenty-five thousand dollars ($25,000) for injury or death to any
            one person, not to exceed fifty thousand dollars ($50,000) per
            occurrence;


                                                 Order No. 09-09-2026 (R-37339) (Corrected)

            b. Property damage insurance providing coverage of at least twenty-
              five thousand dollars ($25,000).
           c. In lieu of having (a) and (b) above as separate policies, the
              Commission will accept a minimum of seventy-five thousand
              dollars ($75,000) combined single limits coverage for injury or
              death to any one person per occurrence for public liability and
              property damage insurance.

   D. Household Goods Movers are required to have minimum insurance

SECTION 105. PROOF OF INSURANCE

All common and contract carriers of motor vehicles shall, at all times, maintain current insurance
as required in Section 104 above, and shall provide proof of such minimum coverage to the
Commission.

Staff shall have the authority to request updated insurance filing information from the regulated
carrier, their insurance agent, or the carrier’s underwriting company that is on file with the

                                                   Order No. 09-09-2026 (R-37339) (Corrected)
                                                                                     Page 11
 Commission when renewal or replacement filings have not been made within three (3) years from
the date of the last insurance filing accepted by Staff regardless if the policy has a termination,
expiration, or cancellation date.

The Commission will accept the below forms as proof of insurance.

    A. Public liability and property damage coverage shall be filed with the
       Commission on a Uniform Certificate of Insurance Form E and
       cancellation of public liability and property damage filings shall be made
       on a Uniform Notice of Cancellation of Motor Carrier Insurance Policies
       Form K filing.

    B. Workman’s Compensation coverage shall be filed with the Commission
       on an ACORD Certificate of Insurance or its equivalent.

    C. Motor Truck cargo insurance shall be filed with the Commission on a
       Uniform Motor Carrier Cargo Certificate of Insurance Form H filing and
       cancellation of cargo insurance filings shall be made on a Uniform Notice
       of Cancellation of Motor Carrier Insurance Policies Form K filing.

    D. Surety bonds shall be filed with the Commission as an original executed
       “License and Permit” bond or irrevocable letter of credit from an FDIC
       financial institute.

SECTION 106. FILING REQUIREMENTS

   A. Initial, renewal, and cancellation insurance filings may be submitted by
      mail, email or electronically, with the exception of initial original Surety
      Bonds which shall be mailed. Filings by Fax are not permitted.

   B. All insurance filings require at least a thirty (30) days’ notice for
      cancellation. Such notices and filings are to be received by the Commission
      no less than 30 days prior to the date of cancellation.

   C. All submissions of Forms E, H, and K shall only be made by the authorized
      underwriting company.

   D. All ACORD Certificates shall only be submitted by the carrier’s insurance
      agent.

   E. The submission of surety bonds and/or continuation certificates may be
      made by the motor carrier, insurance agent, or authorized underwriting
      company.

   F. When a motor carrier is applying for any type of authority with LPSC, the
      motor carrier’s name and address on all insurance filings must match the
      motor carrier’s application for authority.

   G. For insurance renewals, the name and address on a registered motor
      carrier’s insurance filing must match the current name and address of the
      motor carrier that is on file with the Commission.

   H. When a lapse in insurance filings with the Commission occurs, motor
      carriers shall submit: (1) A notarized affidavit providing details of the lapse
      in filings with the Commission, including documentation showing no lapse
      in insurance coverage; or (2) A letter from the motor carrier’s Insurance
      Agent with documentation showing no lapse in insurance coverage.

SECTION 107. VIOLATIONS

When a Common or Contract Carrier by Motor Vehicle is in violation of any of the Rules contained
herein, including an actual lapse in insurance coverage, said carrier is subject to citation and could

 be fined by the Commission, after an open hearing, of not less than one hundred dollars ($100)
and no more than ten thousand ($10,000) for each violation.

Carriers not operating during the lapsed insurance coverage will not be cited by the Commission,
provided the carrier submits a notarized affidavit stating that the motor carrier was not operating
any vehicles within Louisiana during the lapsed period.

In addition to a fine, the Commission, pursuant to Louisiana Revised Statute 45:166(A), may
amend, suspend, or revoke (in whole or in part) a carrier’s certificate or permit with the
Commission, after notice and an open hearing, for failure to comply with these Rules.

Staff may seek the cancellation of a carrier’s authority, after due notice and hearing, based on the
carrier’s failure to update insurance filings with the Commission if the carrier has failed to update
the insurance filings within three (3) years, or if the motor carrier fails to update insurance filings
based upon Commission Staff’s request for updated filings within three (3) years from the date of
the last insurance filing accepted by Staff.

A citation fee as outlined in Commission General Order dated June 7, 2006 shall also be assessed
to any carrier who is issued a citation for any violation set forth in these Rules.
